name: X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 4

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 4

criteria.description: Presence of a family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait disturbance and limb incoordination
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the implicated gene on the X chromosome
Exclusion of other causes of spinocerebellar ataxia by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Electrophysiological evidence of peripheral neuropathy or cerebellar dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia, positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance, and genetic confirmation of pathogenic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires molecular genetic testing due to phenotypic overlap with other SCAs.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of ataxia
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar atrophy predominantly affecting the vermis and hemispheres
genetic: Pathogenic mutation in the gene associated with X-linked spinocerebellar ataxia type 4
other: Nerve conduction studies showing sensory-motor axonal neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with more prominent pyramidal signs
Presence of cardiomyopathy and diabetes mellitus
More prominent sensory ataxia and absent deep tendon reflexes

redFlags: Rapid progression of ataxia over weeks
Presence of systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or fever
references: Orphanet: X-linked Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 4 - ORPHA:85292
Recent advances in the genetics of spinocerebellar ataxias, Lancet Neurol. 2023
